newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan group calls for lifting ban on newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan group calls for lifting ban on newspaper.

text.p: A Moroccan human rights group on Thursday denounced a ban on a popular newspaper and urged the government to lift it.

The Moroccan Human Rights Association (AMDH), one of Morocco's three active rights groups, said the Interior Ministry banned Al-Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi, a weekly political newspaper, last week without explanation.
"We consider the ban decision, which was issued with no respect of Morocco's legal proceedings, is a political power abuse," the AMDH said in statement faxed to an international news agency.
The editor, Mustapha Alaoui, was summoned last week to police headquarters and told that the newspaper was banned but given no reason.
The ban, signed by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, was effective from November 20, he said.
Officials at the Interior Ministry declined to comment.
The AMDH said the decision "violates the freedom of speech, the constitution and principles of human rights in Morocco...It should be withdrawn as soon as possible".
The independent newspaper has a circulation of more than 100,000 copies a week.
Morocco has a dozen daily newspapers and four weeklies, half of them published in Arabic and the other half in French. Most are mouthpieces for political parties.
